labels.label: def:syracuse_cycle_period_denote
labels.notes:
Unmarked and partial. That is correct: the row rests on reading a misprint.

LITERAL READING. ascIdxLit and descIdxLit (UpperBounds.lean:170, :173) take l.271 at its word: a_i := T^i(x_0) = x_i, with x_i = T^{i mod n}(x_0) (cyclePt, :167), which is the right extension of a cycle to i in Z. The degeneracy is real. On the cycle (-1) both sets are empty. On the cycle (1) every index is 'ascending' although a_i(1) = nu2(4) = 2 (literal_neg_one, literal_one). The reading a_i = a_i(x_0) = nu2(3T^i(x_0)+1) (def:ring_define_2) is the only one that fits the rest of the section: l.277 uses 2^{a_i}, and A_u^n(a) takes a in (N*)^Z (l.81).

READ FORM. ascIdx and descIdx (:128, :131) are {i | alpha i = 1} and {i | 1 < alpha i}, verbatim, for any alpha. On a cycle of Z, alpha is any n-periodic extension of (a_k(x))_k. That extension exists (aPer) and is unique, and it is >= 1 (one_le_of_cycle), so the two sets partition Z. a_zero_eq_one_iff_lt_T (:148) is correct: a_0 = 1 gives T y = (3y+1)/2 > y, and a_0 >= 2 gives T y <= (3y+1)/4 < y for y > 0. The index convention (OQ-63 (b)) only shifts the sets by one, as disclosed.

labels.label: lem:syracuse_cycle_n__n_
labels.notes:
Unmarked and partial. That is correct: both displays are false as printed under both readings of OQ-43.

PRINTED FORMS. deltaPrinted (:319) is l.277's right-hand side term by term: sum over k in [1, n-1] of 3^{n-1-k} 2^{sum_{t<k} a_{i+t}} (2^{a_{i+k}} - 2^{a_i}), so the exponent is a_i + ... + a_{i+k-1}. Delta (:312) is A_{i+1}^n - A_i^n with the printed Aun (Base.lean:287). DeltaAlt (:315) is the same with AunAlt (Rep.lean:292, OQ-43).

syracuse_cycle_n_printed_false (:518) negates the lemma with all its hypotheses: for every x in Z, n > 0, T^[n] x = x, every n-periodic alpha with alpha k = a_k(x) on N, and every i in Z. The quantifier over cycles of Z is the paper's (§ 1: 'u_0 in Z'; § 2 works over Z, and the known cycles include negative ones). The witness is not a strawman. The cycle (-5,-7) has a = (1,2) (seq12_eq_a). There A = 14, 20 and A' = 5, 7, so Delta_0 = 6 and Delta'_0 = 2, while the printed side is 2^1(2^2 - 2^1) = 4. I recomputed all of this by exact integer arithmetic.

l.280 (syracuse_cycle_n_asc_printed_false, :537) adds the hypothesis a_i = 1 and takes both readings of 'k in D', as i+k in D (deltaPrintedAsc) and literally as a_k > 1 (deltaPrintedAscLit). Both give 4 at the same point, against 6 and 2.

The failure is structural, not one bad point. deltaPrinted_eq (printed = 2^{a_i} Delta'_i) and deltaPrinted_ne_of_minimal show that the display fails at every i for every a >= 1 of minimal period n >= 2. So no reading of the index convention rescues it.

TRUE FORMS. They are proved unmarked and assume less than the paper:
- DeltaAlt_eq needs no hypothesis at all.
- Delta_eq (3^{n-k}) needs only periodicity.
- DeltaAlt_eq_asc and Delta_eq_asc need a >= 1, which holds on a cycle.
I checked all four identities, Delta = 3 Delta' and printed = 2^{a_i} Delta' numerically on 3000 random periodic sequences (n <= 7, a in [1,4], i in [-3,3]), with no failure. This confirms the planner's [r] note.

One small imprecision in the REPORT prose: 'it equals either difference only where Delta'_i = 0' needs a_i >= 1. It holds for the paper's a in (N*)^Z, so it is harmless.

labels.label: lem:syracuse_cycle
labels.notes:
Unmarked and partial. That is correct, and leaving it unmarked is the right call even though the implication holds as printed.

THE IMPLICATION. syracuse_cycle (:616) and syracuse_cycle_alt (:605) prove a_i = a_{i+1} = 1 => Delta_i ~_S Delta_{i+1} under both readings of OQ-43, with the explicit factor 2/3 = 2^1 3^{-1} in S. They assume only that alpha is n-periodic: no cycle and no a >= 1, which is weaker than the paper. The identity behind them is 2^{a_u} A'_{u+1} = 3A'_u + 2^P - 3^n (two_pow_mul_AunAlt_succ). I checked 3 Delta_i = 2 Delta_{i+1} numerically wherever a_i = a_{i+1} = 1. A probe instantiated both theorems at seq17, i = 0, where Delta and Delta' are nonzero, so the hypotheses are not vacuous.

~_S. It is used at l.286, l.301 and l.318-320 and defined nowhere, as the REPORT says. The reading SEquiv, x = s y with s in S, in Q, is consistent with its later uses, which strip a common factor 2^a 3^b. It is an equivalence relation (sEquiv_equivalence). Because S is positive, this is the strictest natural reading, so the proof carries over to a looser one.

THE 'let m' CLAUSE. Reading it as an assertion is fair. 'let m = GCD(A_i : i in Z) = 2^{p_n} - 3^n' is a chain of equalities: it names m and asserts GCD(A_i) = 2^{p_n} - 3^n. If the clause is read as a recall of prop:have_gcd_n__l_k, the printed statement still contains the same false equality.
- For AunAlt: dvd_iff_dvd_AunAlt_of_cycle proves it up to sign, and gcd_AunAlt_of_pos proves it as printed for x > 0. gcd_AunAlt_printed_false refutes it at the cycle (-1), where the GCD is 1 and 2 - 3 = -1. This is the normalized-GCD convention that the T-syr-cycle-gcd audit accepted (l.164, l.189), and it is the same finding as OQ-63 (a).
- For Aun: every A_u = 2^{a_u} A'_{u+1} is even and 2^{p_n} - 3^n is odd, so it fails on every cycle, signed, normalized and up to sign (gcd_Aun_ne_of_cycle, not_dvd_iff_dvd_Aun_of_cycle).

WHY UNMARKED. Two things block a mark, independently of how the clause is read. First, ~_S is undefined, so a mark would certify a reading the paper does not settle (kb/0006). Second, the clause is false as printed. The REPORT puts both questions to the author and records that a ruling could mark the implication. Under-marking claims nothing.

labels.label: cor:intertwined_i_
labels.notes:
Unmarked and partial. That is correct: 'intertwined' is undefined, and the printed equality with m = 2^{p_n} - 3^n is false.

TRUE FORMS. They are stronger than the paper, because they drop the 'intertwined' hypothesis:
- intertwined_alt (:891) and intertwined_aun (:1011) hold for every n-periodic a >= 1 with n >= 1, at every base point c. For the gcd convention of OQ-63 (b), the base point c = -1 is the one that matters.
- corGcdAlt_of_cycle gives |2^{p_n(x)} - 3^n| on every cycle of Z, with corGcdAlt_of_pos and corGcdAlt_of_neg for the two signs.
- corGcd_eq_gcd_Aun gives GCD(A_i).
corGcd and corGcdAlt (:1059, :1054) are gcd(A_0, gcd over D ∩ [0, n-1] of Delta_{i-1}). This is the paper's A_0 ∧ ⋀_{i in D} Delta_{i-1}: ∧ is gcd, as at l.299, and the two agree by periodicity (forall_of_range). The universal-property forms quantify over all i in Z with a_i > 1. Numerically, on 3000 random periodic sequences and base points c in [-2,2], the corollary's gcd equals gcd(A_u) under both readings, with no failure. Probes instantiated intertwined_alt_cycle, corGcdAlt_of_cycle, intertwined_aun and corGcd_eq_gcd_Aun at the cycles (-5,-7) and (-17).

PRINTED FORM. intertwined_printed_false (:1140) takes the reading of 'intertwined' as a parameter I, with the single hypothesis that I holds of the alternating pattern 2Z / 2Z+1. Any reasonable sense of 'intertwined' admits that pattern, and ascIdx_descIdx_seq12 shows it is the pattern of the cycle (-5,-7). At that cycle m = 2^3 - 9 = -1, corGcdAlt = 1 (A'_0 = 5, Delta'_0 = 2) and corGcd = 2 (A_0 = 14, Delta_0 = 6). Under the OQ-43 reading the failure is a sign failure only, which the REPORT states (m for x > 0, -m for x < 0). Under Aun it fails up to sign as well.

NUMERICS (Finding 6). The orbit of -17 is -17, -25, -37, -55, -41, -61, -91, so a = (1,1,1,2,1,1,4) and p_7 = 11. 2^{p_n} - 3^n is 1, -1, -1, -139 on the cycles of 1, -1, -5, -17. I recomputed the gcds:
- corGcdAlt is 1, 1, 1, 139;
- corGcd is 4, 2, 2, 278;
- gcd(A_i) is 4, 2, 2, 278.
The correction of the planner's '2m for Aun' is right: at the cycle (1), a = 2, every A_i = 4 and m = 1, so the value is 4m (four_cycles_two_m_false).

notes:
There is no finding, major or minor. All four rows are correctly unmarked and partial. Every reading is disclosed in the checklist, the SCOPE and the REPORT: a_i as a_i(x_0), both OQ-43 readings, both readings of 'k in D', ~_S as SEquiv, the 'let m' clause as an assertion, 'intertwined' as a parameter, and the normalized GCD.

Each *_printed_false negates the paper's own statement with its hypotheses. The quantifier ranges over the cycles of Z, and the universal over the periodic extension alpha costs nothing. The witnesses are genuine cycles. Every number checks by exact arithmetic:
- (-5,-7): Delta_0 = 6, Delta'_0 = 2, printed 4;
- the orbit of -17: -17, -25, -37, -55, -41, -61, -91;
- the gcds: 1, 1, 1, 139 and 4, 2, 2, 278.
The planner's [r] numerics are confirmed, apart from '2m for Aun', which the closer correctly refutes at the cycle (1).

The true forms assume no more than the paper. They drop the cycle, and for the corollary the 'intertwined' hypothesis, and they are not vacuous.

Observations for the master need no fix. (1) The scaffold root does not import SyracuseScaffold.UpperBounds, as the closer discloses. (2) Some helpers appear both under a label and in extra_decls. Take the anchors from the label lists: DeltaAlt_eq, Delta_eq, syracuse_cycle(_alt), dvd_iff_dvd_AunAlt_of_cycle, intertwined_alt, intertwined_aun, corGcdAlt_of_cycle, corGcd_eq_gcd_Aun, and the *_printed_false. (3) Generic names (periodic_emod, forall_of_step, forall_of_range) are general-purpose lemmas in namespace Syracuse. They clash with nothing now; renaming is optional at graduation. UpperBounds.lean can graduate as is.
